title: NY State Assembly · District 42
area: Ditmas Park, Flatbush, East Flatbush and Midwood, Brooklyn.

context.text: Incumbent Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn and Republican nominee Herman Hall both advanced from their respective primaries, scheduled for June 23, 2026, without appearing on the ballot after the primaries were canceled.

summary.text: Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Assembly District 42, in office since January 2015. An engineer, investment banker and former math teacher by background, she is the Assembly Majority Whip, chairs the Subcommittee on Oversight of Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprises (MWBEs), and has also served as chair of the Kings County Democratic Party. She is running for re-election in November 2026.

background.text: Born and raised in Flatbush, Brooklyn, the daughter of Haitian immigrants; according to her official biography, she is the first Haitian American woman elected in New York City. Her biography also says she attended LaGuardia School of Music and Performing Arts.

Holds an MBA from Northwestern University's Kellogg School of Management, an MS in electrical engineering from Illinois Institute of Technology, a BS in electrical engineering from SUNY Buffalo, and a BS in mathematics in secondary education and a BT in electrical engineering from Buffalo State College; her biography also says she graduated from Brooklyn Law School in 2024 with a J.D.

Before public office, worked as a math teacher in the New York City public school system, a telecommunications engineer (with assignments in Japan and China), and an investment banker, according to her official biography; she was named an MIT Fellow in the Mel King Co-Lab Project.

Was elected a Democratic District Leader in 2010 and served as a board member of Habitat for Humanity, taking part in a 2011 home-building effort in Leogane, Haiti, according to her official biography.
Ran for the District 42 Assembly seat in 2014, defeating three candidates in the Democratic primary; she assumed office on January 1, 2015, succeeding Rhoda Jacobs.
Since becoming a legislator in 2015, has introduced more than 200 bills, 34 of which have become law, and co-sponsored more than 250 others, according to her official biography.

Serves as Assembly Majority Whip and chairs the MWBE oversight subcommittee, which her biography credits with sponsored laws enacted in 2022 on MWBE program fraud, refinancing through the MWBE lending program and state contract spending thresholds; also sits on the Housing, Education, Governmental Operations, Health, Higher Education and Ways and Means committees.

Sponsored the Jonah Bichotte Cowan Law, named for her late son, which sets requirements for hospital treatment of women who come in with concerns about pre-term labor; her biography also describes her role in establishing the Haitian Studies Institute at Brooklyn College and the Little Haiti Cultural and Business District in Flatbush.

Was nominated chair of the Kings County Democratic County Committee in January 2020, according to Ballotpedia. In October 2026, City & State reported that a state Supreme Court justice ruled her term as chair of the Brooklyn Democratic Party's executive committee ended after a September 23 organizational meeting.
Sits on Governor Kathy Hochul's Domestic Violence Advisory Council; lives in Brooklyn with her husband, Edu Hermelyn, and their son, according to her official biography.

priorities.text: Her official biography lists a focus spanning immigration, education, economic development, unemployment, healthcare access, senior citizen centers, affordable housing, school safety, and women's and LGBTQ rights.

As Chair of the MWBE Subcommittee, has prioritized legislation to help minority- and women-owned businesses, including bills on procurement, contracting notice requirements, and anti-fraud protections.

positions.summary: Sponsored A04991, which would prohibit landlords from using an algorithmic device to set residential rent, and A08454, establishing a tenants' bill of rights.

record.text: Chairs the Subcommittee on Oversight of Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprises (MWBEs); also serves on the Education, Governmental Operations, Health, Higher Education, Housing, and Ways and Means committees in the 2025-2026 session.
Sponsored A04991, prohibiting landlords from using an algorithmic device to determine residential rent; referred to the Housing Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.
Sponsored A08454 (print no. A08454A), creating a tenants' bill of rights; amended and recommitted to the Housing Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.

Sponsored A07192, which would prohibit the establishment, incorporation, construction, or capacity increase of for-profit nursing homes; referred to the Health Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.

Sponsored A06839, requiring the Division of Housing and Community Renewal to calculate the period of a tenant's rent reduction for diminished services from the date the diminution actually occurred, rather than from a later filing date; amended twice and advanced to third reading as of May 2026.

candidates.name: Herman Hall

summary.text: Herman Hall is the Republican nominee for NY State Assembly District 42, running against incumbent Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn. The Republican primary was canceled, and he advanced without appearing on the ballot. Ballotpedia lists him as the Conservative Party candidate for the New York State Senate in 2014, and the personal website it links describes a Herman G. Hall as a Caribbean-American journalist, author and magazine publisher.

background.text: Ran for New York State Senate in 2014 as the Conservative Party candidate, losing the general election to incumbent Kevin Parker, according to Ballotpedia.

Hall's personal website, which Ballotpedia links from his candidate page, says Herman G. Hall was born April 26, 1945 in Grenada and is an award-winning journalist, author and publisher of EVERYBODY'S, the Caribbean-American Magazine, who covered the Caribbean and its diaspora for more than 50 years. The site does not mention his Assembly candidacy.

According to that website, he received a National Association of Black Journalists award in 1981 for coverage of the funerals of Prime Minister Eric Williams and Bob Marley, is a former commentator for WLIB and WBLS radio in New York City, and has written books including From Founding Father Alexander Hamilton to Vice President Kamala Harris, Julien Fedon, and Belvedere Estate.

candidates.researchNotes: Hall has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and no campaign website or news coverage of his Assembly candidacy was found. His biography relies on the personal website Ballotpedia links from his candidate page, which does not mention the campaign; no source confirms the details beyond that link.
